parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, and the visitor-facing legal architecture is strong: anti-discrimination covering gender identity and expression, SOGI as a hate-crime aggravator, no documented facility/bathroom exclusion, and a prison protocol placing detainees by gender identity with segmented housing — the opposite of a tier-1 universal exposure. Institutions function (police human-rights unit credited with eliminating reported abuses). Negatives: documented anti-trans violence (a 2023 killing treated as the emblematic case, a 2021 hotel beating), no recorded outcome in the killing, an openly trans police officer litigating institutional discrimination and non-consensual exposure of her private life, and a documented 2024 'year of regression' with far-right pressure and stalled trans legislation. These are isolated incidents plus a cooling climate rather than institutional exclusion or organised targeting. Sits below the 0.85 tier (convictions and demonstrated enforcement of visitor-facing protections) and above 0.65 (uneven remedies), with entry-document practice an open question.
